metadata.notes: These 366 provisional research selections are not 366 verified stories. Source-led discovery and editor approval are separate. No published copy or unpublished graphics included.

limitations: All 366 dates have provisional primary/alternate IDs, not publication-ready vetted stories.
NCEI county/zone records can represent portions of multiday or multijurisdictional events; never sum without verification.
NHC best-track points without local geography/impact evidence are not valid as confirmed landfalls.
Curation quality and Tier 3 labels require human meteorologist editorial judgment.
Most events lack independent corroboration; international and pre-1950 coverage are particularly weak.
No image rights have been cleared in this Phase A research database.
Two sources may originate from the same institution; judge organizational independence separately.
Pass 2 screened two alternate records for each upgraded date (30 leads) but did not independently corroborate those alternate stories.
Same-institution corroboration is labeled and does not establish fully independent sourcing.

25 January 1990 Royal Meteorological Society and Met Office accounts share an underlying Met Office observation record; organizational separation does not mean independent gust measurement corroboration.
28 January 1887 giant-snowflake account held as unresolved historical-date/measurement issue, not upgraded.
Pass 2 continuation to 26 cases retains 8 prior alternate pairs unchanged; no additional independent alternate research is counted in 30 earlier screened leads.
Some dates refer to start of multiday episodes, a transportation closure, or streamflow peak windows rather than a whole-storm culmination. Per-claim dates require human review.
2021 NSW PDF statement text was retrieved but its rendered page could not be inspected; specific map panels and image rights remain unverified.
Great Storm of 1703 assigned Dec 7 in modern Gregorian anniversary, corresponding to November 26 Old Style (Julian); original contemporaneous documents must preserve source calendars.
Flight 242 FAA retelling relies on original NTSB investigation; Wilma NHC and WPC are both NOAA; neither pair is independent underlying event data.
Sept 30, 2019 Montana snow graphic NASA satellite was taken October 1 and snowfall totals refer to several days; source image never treated as September 30 same-day imagery.
Three newly upgraded dates cause or neighbor winter/fire/severe-weather clusters, recorded as editorial diversity warnings, not suppressions.
11 previous pairs of unverified alternates were retained without independent screening; earlier count of 30 screened alternate leads is unchanged.
revision_workflow: Preserve manually curated events and all existing Post Studio copy.
Check source link and dated claims, then independently corroborate before selecting verified status.
Replace weak primary stories with stronger dated events, including international and early historical candidates.
Review every low-quality or same-source-repetition warning; seek non-NOAA primary research sources.
Do not mark approved until full human review and image rights checks are complete.
